items.title: Terri Lyne Carrington interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: Rahsaan Roland Kirk was like one of the first people that I played with.

ctx.x: What about public school? Did you get an opportunity to play in the public school system?

No. I wasn’t very interested in playing in school because growing up I started playing at seven and by the time I was ten I was sitting in with a lot of people when they came through, like Clark Terry and Rahsaan Roland Kirk was like one of the first people that I played with. And I think before I even started playing he got me shaking a tambourine on stage with him and I think saxophone — I played saxophone for a minute when I was five or six. And then the drums. So when I was playing with people like that I…
I can imagine that. It kind of spoiled you I guess. What was it like, do you remember the experience with Rahsaan?
